name: Isolated Partial Vaginal Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Vaginal Agenesis

criteria.description: Partial or segmental absence of the vaginal canal confirmed by clinical examination
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating absence or hypoplasia of vaginal segments with normal uterus
Presence of normally developed uterus and ovaries without associated Mullerian anomalies
No concurrent renal or skeletal malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial vaginal absence on clinical exam and imaging with normal uterine development
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of complete vaginal agenesis and associated syndromic anomalies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary amenorrhea with normal secondary sexual characteristics
searchTerms: no menstruation despite normal puberty signs
primary amenorrhea with normal breasts and hair
no periods but normal secondary sexual features

common.symptomName: Dyspareunia due to vaginal stenosis or shortened vaginal length
searchTerms: painful intercourse due to narrow or short vagina
pain during sex from vaginal stenosis

common.symptomName: Normal secondary sexual characteristics (breast development, pubic hair)
searchTerms: normal breast development and pubic hair
normal puberty signs like breasts and hair

common.symptomName: Normal menstrual bleeding from uterus if vaginal canal is partially patent
searchTerms: normal menstrual bleeding if vaginal opening partly open
periods occur with partial vaginal canal
normal uterine bleeding with partial vaginal patency

occasional.symptomName: Pelvic pain due to hematocolpos or obstructed menstrual flow
searchTerms: pelvic pain from blocked menstrual flow
pain due to trapped menstrual blood

occasional.symptomName: Urinary tract infections secondary to anatomical distortion
searchTerms: UTIs caused by urinary tract distortion
repeated bladder infections due to structure issues

occasional.symptomName: Psychological distress related to sexual dysfunction
searchTerms: psychological issues related to sexual dysfunction
mental health impact of sexual difficulties

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile including FSH, LH, estradiol
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing segmental vaginal agenesis with normal uterus and ovaries
Ultrasound confirming absence of vaginal canal segments
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Normal external genitalia on physical examination
Absence of renal or skeletal anomalies in isolated cases

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of vaginal canal with transverse septum causing obstruction
Menstrual flow obstruction leading to hematocolpos

redFlags: Primary amenorrhea with absent vaginal canal segments
Pelvic pain with signs of hematocolpos or hematometra
Presence of renal or skeletal anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
